elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 2.11: "The licenses granted under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates upon written notice to Commerce One." "CORIO" is defined as Corio Inc. alone, so the extension is not duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Nothing in Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.10 or new 2.11 extends the licences to contractors acting on Corio's behalf; the rationale relies on Section 14.8 subcontracting, which is not part of the operative licence grant and is not rendered. To reach the preferred level the drafter would need to add "and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf" to the Section 2 grants.
2.2 grants a "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license".

2.2 (the fully paid up licence) says "perpetual" but omits "irrevocable"; the word "irrevocable" appears only in 2.1, which is expressly "fee-bearing" rather than paid up. Cure would be inserting "and irrevocable" into 2.2.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 2 contains no subscription licence — 2.1 and 2.2 are perpetual (and, for 2.1, irrevocable) grants — so there is no subscription grant whose termination trigger needs limiting.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: 2.1 and 2.2 are "nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)", and 14.1 permits assignment of the Agreement without consent "in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement", with the Agreement binding on "successors and permitted assigns". The direct-competitor consent carve-out is a qualification but leaves successor transferability materially intact.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: New 2.11 conditions the extension on "written notice to Commerce One", matching the fallback mechanic exactly.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Pre-existing 14.1 allows assignment without consent on merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets, and the Section 2 grants are transferable "in accordance with Section 14.1"; no edit was needed.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Same 14.1 mechanic supports successor transfer at either level.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: new Section 2.11 supplies affiliate coverage on written notice, and retained Section 14.1 already delivers successor transfer in an M&A or substantially-all-assets sale, so the claimed fallback target is fully met.

Preferred level is not reached: (a) no grant language extends the Section 2 licences to contractors acting on Corio's behalf (Section 14.8 subcontracting is not a licence extension), and (b) the fully paid up licence in 2.2 is perpetual but not expressly irrevocable. If the preferred level is later pursued, add "and its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf" to the 2.1/2.2 grants and insert "and irrevocable" in 2.2.

Minimal: a single one-sentence insertion (2.11) addresses the only failing fallback element; no favourable existing language was deleted, no survival tail, expense, procedure or damages boilerplate was added, and the successor element was left to existing 14.1 rather than duplicated with a new assignment exception.

No duplicate coverage: "CORIO" is defined as Corio Inc. only, so affiliates were genuinely outside the grant; a grant to affiliates carries use through their authorised personnel, so no separate personnel edit was needed and none was made.

Preserves intent: the retained "nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)" limb is unaffected because 2.11 is a direct grant by Commerce One rather than a Corio transfer; territory, fee, revenue-share and 2.10 expansion mechanics survive unchanged. "affiliates" is used in its ordinary lowercase sense, so no dangling defined term is created, though defining "Affiliate" would remove any ambiguity about control thresholds.
Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the edit the clause failed the fallback affiliate element outright with no notice path to add affiliates.
